# Implementation Plan: Verify-and-harden the Anthropic model / gate desync (D-001)

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-25. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan <job_dir>/plan.md`.*

*Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/codex-anthropic-model-persists-without-enable-flag/` @ `2a4eb4ba` (recommended direction **D-001: verify-and-harden**).*

> **Target repo:** the **codex submodule** at `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs` (inner submodule `527027282e`, wrapper `5f9dc1105e`, version `0.141.0-copilot-api.3`). All code/test edits land inside that submodule and ship as a submodule commit + a codexu pointer bump. Plan deliverables (this file) live in codexu at `.ralph/jobs/codex-anthropic-model-persists-without-enable-flag/`.

## Overview

The operator-reported bug (2026-06-10): a **persisted** Anthropic model in `~/.codex/config.toml::model` (e.g. `claude-opus-4.8`) plus the Anthropic gate **OFF** (the gate is per-run via `--enable-anthropic` / `features.anthropic_models`, never persisted) made the persisted Claude slug route to the Copilot `/responses` path, which Anthropic models cannot serve, so **every message failed** (`WARN Model metadata for claude-... not found` + `ERROR model not supported`) until the user manually changed the model.

Source verification on the current build (`0.141.0-copilot-api.3`) confirms the **desync path is already closed** by the multi-layer fail-closed reversion that landed AFTER the report (`9345bac3f3` 2026-06-13, `596352d5b3` 2026-06-14; the api-3 tag was re-cut 2026-06-22 and includes them). This task is therefore **verify-and-harden**, not a fresh fix: lock the closed behavior behind a regression test that exercises the **production wrap** + the **session-startup resolution chain** (today's unit tests only exercise the in-isolation decorator via a per-instance test gate), add a guard that the single production model-manager construction site keeps wrapping with `GatedModelsManager`, and update the patch-surface invariant ledger. The one genuine residual gap — the cold-start substitution is **silent** — is captured as an **optional, separable** advisory story the lead can defer (the spawn narrows scope to verify + harden).

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

**The fail-closed reversion is multi-layered and present on api-3 (VERIFIED, cite file:line):**

1. **Gate is a process-global `AtomicBool`, default `false`, never persisted.**
   `model-provider/src/anthropic_gate.rs:12-45` — `AnthropicGate { enabled: AtomicBool::new(false) }`; `install_anthropic_gate(enabled)` (`:37`) stores it at config-build time; `anthropic_models_resolved()` (`:43`) reads it at call sites. Installed once per run from the feature at `core/src/config/mod.rs:2832` (`install_anthropic_gate(features.enabled(Feature::AnthropicModels))`; comment `:2831` "`Feature::AnthropicModels` is the sole authority"). `--enable-anthropic` folds into `-c features.anthropic_models=true` (`cli/src/main.rs:976-977`), so only the **config key** persists; the flag is per-run. This is *why* it desyncs — and is intentional per the experimental-feature design (default off, explicit opt-in per run). `Feature::AnthropicModels` is defined at `features/src/lib.rs:149` (enum) / `:1042` (spec, key `"anthropic_models"`).

2. **Core model-identity reversion (the load-bearing defense).**
   `model-provider/src/copilot/gated_models_manager.rs` — the `GatedModelsManager` decorator:
   - `keep_model_slug(model)` (`:56`) = `anthropic_enabled() || !is_anthropic_model_slug(model)` → when the gate is off, an Anthropic slug is **not** kept.
   - `get_default_model` (`:142-162`): if the supplied model passes `keep_model_slug` + `keep_model`, return it; **otherwise** return `default_model_from_presets(list_models(...))` — i.e. the gate-filtered (non-Anthropic) default. A persisted Claude model with the gate off therefore resolves to the filtered default.
   - `get_model_info` (`:164-180`): same pattern — on a filtered-out slug it builds `model_info` from the **fallback** slug, so even the metadata resolves to a non-Anthropic model.
   - `is_anthropic_model_slug` (`:189-192`) = lowercased `starts_with("claude") || contains("anthropic")`.
   - Existing unit tests (per-instance **test** gate via `wrap_with_test_gate`, `:259-272`): `off_filters_chat_completions_from_all_catalog_reads` (`:282`), `off_does_not_resolve_chat_completions_metadata_for_explicit_model` (`:324`, asserts `slug=="gpt-5.5"` + `used_fallback_model_metadata==true`), `off_replaces_inherited_chat_completions_model_with_filtered_default` (`:337`), `off_replaces_unavailable_anthropic_slug_with_filtered_default` (`:351`), `off_preserves_custom_non_anthropic_slug` (`:365`).

3. **Single production construction site wraps unconditionally.**
   `model-provider/src/copilot.rs::models_manager` (`:108-145`) wraps BOTH branches with `GatedModelsManager::wrap(...)`: the config-supplied-catalog branch over `StaticModelsManager` (`:123`) and the live `/models` branch over `OpenAiModelsManager` (`:140`). `GatedModelsManager::wrap` installs `AnthropicGate::Global` (`gated_models_manager.rs:48-54`), which reads the process-global gate live. This is the chokepoint the guard test protects.

4. **Session-startup resolution chain (the production consumer).**
   `core/src/session/mod.rs:564-574` — `model = models_manager.get_default_model(&config.model, refresh_strategy)` (`:564`) then `model_info = models_manager.get_model_info(model.as_str(), …)` (`:572`). The resolved `model_info.slug` is what builds the outbound request at `core/src/client.rs:814-815` (`ResponsesApiRequest { model: model_info.slug.clone(), … }`). So `config.model = "claude-opus-4.8"` + gate off → `get_default_model` returns the non-Claude fallback → `get_model_info(<fallback>)` returns the real fallback info → `request.model` is the fallback, never the Claude slug. **The bad request can no longer be built.**

5. **TUI cold-start reversion.**
   `tui/src/app_server_session.rs::bootstrap_default_model` (`:1260-1274`) keeps `configured_model` only when NOT `is_unavailable_anthropic_model` (`:1276-1281` = an Anthropic slug absent from the gate-filtered `available_models`); otherwise it falls back to the catalog default. Unit tests at `:1862` (`bootstrap_default_model_replaces_unavailable_claude_config_model`), `:1872`, `:1885`.

6. **Routing companion (defense-in-depth).**
   `core/src/chat_transport.rs::effective_wire_api_gated` (`:68-77`) forces a chat-hinted model to `ChatCompletions` ONLY when the gate is on; otherwise the provider wire (Responses). This only changes the *wire route*, not the *slug* — the slug reversion in (2) is what actually prevents the bad request, but with the slug reverted to a `ProviderDefault` model the route is correctly Responses with a **valid** model.

7. **Stale-cache vector already defended.**
   Patch-surface **Invariant 50** (`c7cf5413b0`): the Copilot `models_cache.json` identity includes `anthropic_models=<resolved gate>` (`copilot_models_endpoint.rs::cache_identity`, tested by `cache_identity_tracks_resolved_anthropic_gate` `:582-604`). A gate-off run does not read a gate-on run's cache, so the "stale cache from a prior gate-on run" path is already closed — a dedicated regression test there would mostly re-assert Invariant 50.

**The one genuine residual gap (silent substitution).** The live `/experimental` toggle path messages the user ("Model changed to {x} because the previous model is no longer available.", `tui/src/chatwidget/settings.rs:237-240` via `add_info_message`). The **cold-start** path is silent: at session startup the two-step resolution "launders" the fallback signal — `get_default_model` returns the already-reverted slug, then `get_model_info(<reverted slug>)` returns a real lookup with `used_fallback_model_metadata == false`, so `core/src/session/turn_context.rs::maybe_emit_unknown_model_warning_for_turn` (`:854-867`, which fires only on `used_fallback_model_metadata`) does **not** fire. The user silently runs on a fallback model with `config.toml::model` still saying `claude-…`. This is a UX gap, not a correctness gap (messages now succeed).

**Invariant ledger.** The reversion is registered as patch-surface **Invariant 39** ("D-002 Anthropic opt-in gate is default-off across all four user-facing selection/routing surfaces"; `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md:877`). Its break-it list already names "let inherited Claude configs survive `get_default_model`"; its enforcing-test column lists the `gated_models_manager.rs` + `copilot_models_endpoint.rs` + `chat_transport.rs` tests. Per fork tenant #3 (`codex/CLAUDE.md`), any new enforcing test must be added to this mapping in the same commit.

### Technical Constraints

- **Copilot-provider end-to-end test fixture does NOT exist.** The WIP copilot-client integration tests (`configure_copilot_session_for_tests` + the `/responses`→wiremock side-channel) were **removed in the v0.140.0 rebase** because the fork infra was never committed (`core/tests/suite/client.rs:1059-1065`; re-adding is tracked as `codex-rebase-debt-fix-client-copilot-fixture`). Generic `test_codex()` uses `CodexAuth::from_api_key` + the **OpenAI** provider, which never touches the gate/`GatedModelsManager` path. **Therefore a full `core/suite` headless-`exec` test asserting the outbound `/responses` body model is NOT feasible today** without first rebuilding that fixture. The feasible locking test lives at the **`model-provider` crate level**, against the real production `CopilotModelProvider::models_manager()` wrap.
- **The gate is a process-global `AtomicBool`, so gate-driving tests need serialization (F-001, F-002).** `serial_test` IS defined at the workspace root (`codex-rs/Cargo.toml:417`, `serial_test = "3.2.0"`) and is already a dev-dep of `core`/`app-server`/`tui` — but it is **NOT yet a dev-dep of `model-provider`** (`model-provider/Cargo.toml:42-46` has only `pretty_assertions`, `serde_json`, `tokio`, `wiremock`). The impl MUST first add `serial_test = { workspace = true }` to `model-provider/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies]`, otherwise the new `#[serial_test::serial]` tests will not compile. (`serial_test 3.2.0` is already resolved in `Cargo.lock` via the other crates, so this edge should NOT change `Cargo.lock` / require a Bazel-lock update — verify `cargo check` leaves `Cargo.lock` unchanged; if it does change, run `just bazel-lock-update` + `just bazel-lock-check` per the codex-rs AGENTS.md.) New gate-driving tests MUST: (a) be `#[serial_test::serial]`; (b) call `install_anthropic_gate(false)` at the START (not only the end) with minimal code between set and assert; (c) reset to `false` at the END. Additionally, the existing `cache_identity_tracks_resolved_anthropic_gate` (`copilot_models_endpoint.rs:582-604`) flips the global gate `false→true→false` and is currently **un-serialized** — add `#[serial_test::serial]` to it too so it cannot race the new tests. Prefer asserting the **off** state (the global default) so a missed `#[serial]` cannot corrupt another test.
- **`CopilotModelProvider` is test-constructable in-crate.** `CopilotModelProvider::new(info: ModelProviderInfo, auth_manager: Option<Arc<AuthManager>>)` (`copilot.rs:64`) is `pub(crate)`; there is already a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `copilot.rs:189`. `models_manager(codex_home, Some(catalog))` uses `StaticModelsManager::new(auth_manager, catalog)` (`models-manager/src/manager.rs:245`) → no network. New tests can construct a provider, supply a 2-entry catalog (`gpt-5.5` ProviderDefault `is_default` + `claude-opus-4.8` ChatCompletions), and drive the resolution.
- **Fork conventions** (`codex/external/repos/codex-patched/AGENTS.md`): inline `format!` args; method references over closures; exhaustive `match`; tests use `pretty_assertions::assert_eq` and compare whole objects; put a new test module in a sibling `*_tests.rs` with `#[path = "..."]` ONLY when introducing a new module (do not rewrite existing inline `mod tests`); keep crate API surface minimal (no new `pub` test-only helpers). Run `just fmt` + `just test -p codex-model-provider` after edits; run `just fix -p codex-model-provider` for clippy. `cargo check --workspace` (~6 min) is the typecheck gate. Do NOT add the `// SANDBOX PATCH` markers/tests in a way that widens the crate API.

## Approach

### Architecture

Keep the gate authoritative and `config.toml::model` untouched on disk (D-001 decision; re-enabling `--enable-anthropic` restores the persisted Claude preference). Add tests that exercise the **production** wrap + the **session-startup resolution chain** at the only feasible layer (`model-provider` crate), and extend the patch-surface Invariant 39 mapping. No production code change is required for the verify-and-harden core (US-001–US-003). The optional advisory (US-004) is the only behavior change and is separable.

### Implementation Strategy

1. **US-001** — locking regression test that reproduces the operator scenario through the production wrap + resolution chain (gate off + persisted Claude → non-Claude fallback). New tests in `model-provider` (add the `serial_test` dev-dep first).
2. **US-002** — wrap-guard test: the production `models_manager()` config-catalog branch returns a Claude-filtering (gated) manager when the gate is off, PLUS a static guard in `codex/scripts/audit_invariants.sh` that fails if EITHER wrap site (`copilot.rs:123` config-catalog, `copilot.rs:140` live `/models`) stops returning `GatedModelsManager::wrap(...)` — so the network-bound online branch is guarded too (F-003).
3. **US-003** — extend patch-surface **Invariant 39** (`codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md:877`) enforcing-test list with the US-001 test names AND the new `audit_invariants.sh` check (F-005) + a one-line verify note (desync closed on api-3, key file:line). Doc-only.
4. **US-004 (DEFERRED — out of default impl scope)** — cold-start + exec advisory when a persisted Anthropic model is reverted because the gate is off. Behavior change touching `core` + `tui` (snapshot test). **Do NOT implement in the default ship** (F-006); file as a separate follow-up unless the operator explicitly opts in.

### Commit & ship layering (nested submodules — F-004)

This task spans the inner submodule, the codex wrapper, and codexu. Commit in this order:

1. **Inner submodule** `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/` (the `codex-rs` workspace): `model-provider/Cargo.toml` (add `serial_test` dev-dep) + the US-001/US-002 tests + (only if it changed) `Cargo.lock`. Commit here first; this is where the topic branch the skill manages lives for code edits.
2. **codex wrapper** `codex/`: `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` (Invariant 39 update, US-003) + `scripts/audit_invariants.sh` (the new wrap-site check, US-002) + the submodule **gitlink bump** pointing at the commit from step 1.
3. **codexu** (lead-owned at ship time): bump the `codex/` pointer to the wrapper commit from step 2.

Do not mix uncommitted inner-submodule edits into the wrapper commit — the wrapper commit can only record the gitlink SHA. The lead handles the FF-merge + pushes (ask-before-pushing); the impl member's scope is the local commits on the topic branch.

(Prefer extending an existing inline test module; if a new module is warranted, use a sibling `copilot_tests.rs` with `#[path]`.)

## Scope

### In Scope

- VERIFY (documented above, with file:line citations) that the gate-off + persisted-Anthropic-model desync path is closed on `0.141.0-copilot-api.3`.
- HARDEN: a `model-provider`-level locking regression test (US-001) + a production-wrap guard (US-002) + the Invariant 39 ledger update (US-003).
- All changes confined to the codex submodule (+ a codexu submodule-pointer bump at ship time, handled by the lead).

### Out of Scope

- Rebuilding the removed Copilot end-to-end `/responses` test fixture (`codex-rebase-debt-fix-client-copilot-fixture`) — the heavier headless-`exec` outbound-body test is blocked on it and is explicitly deferred.
- A dedicated stale-`models_cache.json` regression test — already defended by Invariant 50; would mostly re-assert it.
- Changing the persisted-vs-runtime model policy (D-002 "couple-the-persists" / D-003 "selection-time guard") — both were rejected by the brainstorm in favor of D-001.
- Rewriting `config.toml::model` on disk.
- **US-004 advisory is DEFERRED** — included as a separable, fully-specified story but NOT part of the default verify-and-harden ship. The default impl scope is **US-001 + US-002 + US-003 only**. Do not implement US-004 unless the operator explicitly opts in (F-006).

## Risk Areas

- **Global-gate test flakiness.** Mitigated by `#[serial_test::serial]` + `install_anthropic_gate(false)` at BOTH start and end + asserting the off (default) state. `serial_test` must first be added to `model-provider`'s `[dev-dependencies]` (it is a workspace dep but not yet wired to this crate — F-001), and the existing un-serialized `cache_identity_tracks_resolved_anthropic_gate` test must also get `#[serial]` (F-002) or it can race the new tests. If a reviewer prefers zero global-state risk, US-001/US-002 can also be expressed with the per-instance `wrap_with_test_gate` — but that would NOT exercise the production `GatedModelsManager::wrap`/`AnthropicGate::Global` path, which is the whole point of the new test (existing tests already cover the per-instance decorator). Recommendation: keep at least one test on the production global wrap.
- **US-001 is a model-provider-level lock, not a session/request-boundary lock (F-007).** US-001 manually replays the two-step `session/mod.rs` resolution; a future refactor that builds the request from `config.model` directly (bypassing `get_default_model`/`get_model_info`) would still pass US-001/US-002. The true session→request-boundary test needs the removed Copilot fixture (out of scope). Mitigation: US-001 covers the production wrap + the exact resolution sequence today; an OPTIONAL core-level no-network stretch test around the provider/session model-manager handoff could narrow this gap further if a feasible seam exists — left as an Open Question rather than a requirement.
- **`ModelInfo` has no `is_default` field (F-008).** Defaulting is derived at the `ModelPreset` level (`default_model_from_presets` finds `ModelPreset.is_default`, else `.first()`). The catalog must make `gpt-5.5` the surviving fallback by ordering it first (mirror the existing helper `gated_models_manager.rs:259-272`), NOT by setting a nonexistent `ModelInfo.is_default`.
- **Test duplication.** The existing `gated_models_manager.rs` tests already prove the decorator in isolation. US-001 must add NEW coverage (production `models_manager()` wrap + the two-step `get_default_model`→`get_model_info` chain as `session/mod.rs` performs it), not restate `off_replaces_inherited_…`.
- **Guard expressiveness.** Prefer the behavioral test (US-002) as primary; the static guard in `audit_invariants.sh` must use the existing `require_file_pattern`/`grep -c` style (`audit_invariants.sh:40-48`) anchored on the two `GatedModelsManager::wrap(` occurrences / `// SANDBOX PATCH` markers at `copilot.rs:123,140` (e.g. assert the count of `GatedModelsManager::wrap(` in `copilot.rs` is ≥ 2), not free-text matching.
- **US-004 surface creep.** The advisory spans `core` + `tui` + requires an `insta` snapshot and must compare resolved-vs-configured model explicitly (the `used_fallback_model_metadata` signal is laundered away at startup — see Research Findings). Keep it separable; do not let it block the core ship.
- **Submodule build discipline.** `cargo check --workspace` (~6 min) is the local gate; `cargo build --release` / `cargo test --workspace` are CI-only (90+ min locally). Run `just test -p codex-model-provider` for the touched crate. If adding `serial_test` to `model-provider` changes `Cargo.lock` (it should not — already resolved via core/app-server/tui), run `just bazel-lock-update` + `just bazel-lock-check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- VERIFY: plan documents, with file:line citations on `0.141.0-copilot-api.3`, that gate-off + persisted-Anthropic-model resolves to a non-Anthropic model before the request is built (so `/responses` never receives a Claude slug). *(satisfied by this plan's Research Findings.)*
- HARDEN US-001: the impl first adds `serial_test = { workspace = true }` to `model-provider/Cargo.toml [dev-dependencies]`, then a new `model-provider` test drives `CopilotModelProvider::new(...).models_manager(codex_home, Some(catalog))` with the gate OFF and replicates `session/mod.rs:564-573` for `config.model = "claude-opus-4.8"` (`get_default_model(&Some("claude-opus-4.8"))` then `get_model_info(<result>)`), and asserts the resolved model slug is the non-Anthropic fallback (`gpt-5.5`) AND its `wire_route == ModelWireRoute::ProviderDefault` (i.e. a valid Responses request). The catalog makes `gpt-5.5` the surviving fallback by ordering it first (NOT via a nonexistent `ModelInfo.is_default`). The test is `#[serial_test::serial]`, calls `install_anthropic_gate(false)` at start and end, and the existing `cache_identity_tracks_resolved_anthropic_gate` test is also marked `#[serial]`.
- HARDEN US-002: a new `model-provider` test asserts the production `models_manager(Some(catalog))` config-catalog branch filters Claude from `list_models()`/`try_list_models()` when the gate is off (proving the wrap is present, not bypassed); AND `bash codex/scripts/audit_invariants.sh` fails if either wrap site (`copilot.rs:123`, `:140`) stops returning `GatedModelsManager::wrap(...)` (e.g. assert ≥ 2 `GatedModelsManager::wrap(` occurrences in `copilot.rs`). This makes the network-bound online branch testably guarded, not just commented.
- US-003: patch-surface Invariant 39's enforcing-test column lists the US-001/US-002 test names and a one-line verify note; `codex/docs/implementation/patch-surface.md` remains internally consistent.
- All new tests pass via `just test -p codex-model-provider`; `cargo check --workspace` is green; `just fmt` clean.
- *(US-004, only if opted in)* a one-time advisory appears on TUI cold start AND exec/headless when a persisted Anthropic model is reverted because the gate is off; `config.toml::model` is unchanged; covered by a TUI `insta` snapshot + a core unit/integration assertion.
